section: Data-driven discovery of novel additives for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition in 3D interconnects > ABSTRACT
text: In advanced electronic manufacturing, additives play a pivotal role in achieving high-quality metal interconnect by enabling precise pattern filling during electrodeposition. Currently, due to complex mechanisms, vast molecular spaces and lack of predictive models, the development of additives still relies on inefficient trial-and-error methods. In this work, a machine learning (ML)-based data-driven framework is developed to accelerate the discovery of cobalt electrodeposition additives.

section: Data-driven discovery of novel additives for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition in 3D interconnects > ABSTRACT
text: In this work, a machine learning (ML)-based data-driven framework is developed to accelerate the discovery of cobalt electrodeposition additives. Focusing on molecular adsorption dynamics at the cobalt elec trolyte interface during electrodeposition, this work employs quantum chemical properties to guide the construction of machine learning models for identifying molecules with ideal adsorption potential. Bayesian optimization is employed to optimize model accuracy by tuning hyperparameters, and SHAP analysis provides interpretable chemical insights.

section: Data-driven discovery of novel additives for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition in 3D interconnects > 1. Introduction
text: As advanced chip manufacturing technologies trend toward miniaturization in the post-Moore's Law era, cobalt (Co) has been proposed as a promising alternative to replace copper (Cu) in advanced semiconductor applications [1–4] due to its superior electrical performance [5,6] and interconnect reliability at the nanoscale [7]. Electrodeposition is the predominant technique for Co interconnects [8,9]. Organic additives are decisive for modulating deposition kinetics and achieving high quality Co interconnects, such as surface planarization [10] and defectfree superfilling in submicron patterns.

section: Data-driven discovery of novel additives for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition in 3D interconnects > 4. Conclusion
text: In summary, this study established a data-driven framework that integrates machine learning with experimental validation to efficiently identify novel, high-efficiency, and low-toxicity nitrogen-containing additives for superconformal cobalt electrodeposition. A comprehensive description of the molecules' physical properties was obtained using RDKit descriptors, and the key feature set was subsequently identified by integrating three feature selection strategies. Among the six evaluated ML models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance for ΔE prediction (R^2= 0.9 4 5).

text: Among the six evaluated ML models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance for ΔE prediction (R^2= 0.9 4 5). These findings provide interpretable insights that can guide the design of additive molecules. The trained model was applied to a commercial molecular database, successfully identifying APZ, MIDCN, and AEP as three promising candidate molecules.
